newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian port Luka Koper to debut Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian port Luka Koper to debut Nov 20.

text.p: Slovenia's only port Luka Koper will list its shares on the primary market on November 20, the Ljubljana bourse said on Thursday.
But the bourse said foreign investors would need state approval before purchasing Luka's shares according to the company's regulations.
The company will list 4.66 million shares with a nominal value of 1,000 tolars per share, representing 33.3 percent of the firm's equity.
The state owns 51 percent of the company and the city of Koper 7.65 percent. Neither the state's nor the city's shares will be listed.
According to Luka's regulations, another 8.05 percent of shares that were sold to employees during the company's privatisation process can not be traded until June 1998 and will thus remain unlisted.
In 1995, sales rose to 7.2 billion tolars ($52.6 million) from 6.2 billion in 1994, while net profit jumped to 877.4 million tolars from 646.1 million.
The bourse said it expected to list the shares of some 10 newly privatised companies by the end of the year.
